title: Governor of Hawaii

context.text: Incumbent Democrat Josh Green is seeking a second term. He won the August 8, 2026 Democratic primary against three other candidates.
Gary Cordery, a contractor, won the August 8, 2026 Republican primary over Hilo businessman Ken Fujiyama; he had finished third in the 2022 Republican primary for governor.

Governors and lieutenant governors run as tickets in the general election. Green's running mate is Kauai Mayor Derek Kawakami; Cordery's is Daniel Anthony. The Hawaii Office of Elections sample general-election ballot lists only these two tickets.

candidates.name: Josh Green
candidates.ballotNote: Running with Kauai Mayor Derek Kawakami for lieutenant governor.

summary.text: Josh Green is the Democratic Governor of Hawaii, a physician who previously served in the state House (2004–2008), the state Senate (2008–2018) and as lieutenant governor (2018–2022). After the 2026 legislative session, 266 of the 267 measures that passed became law and he vetoed one.

background.text: Born in Kingston, New York; B.S. from Swarthmore College and M.D. from Pennsylvania State University.
Served in the Hawaii House (2004–2008) and Senate (2008–2018), then as the 15th Lieutenant Governor of Hawaii (2018–2022) under David Ige.
Took office as governor on December 5, 2022.

priorities.text: Cost of living, citing a state tax cut for middle-income residents.
priorities.quote: In his first term, Governor Josh Green delivered the biggest tax cut for the middle class in Hawaii state history.

priorities.text: Housing costs, described on his campaign site as a focus.
priorities.quote: Governor Green is also bringing down housing costs for everyone in Hawaii.

priorities.text: Homelessness, with a campaign claim of record state investment since 2022.

record.text: Signed HB 2404 (Act 46, 2024), a tax cut for working families that raises the standard deduction and lowers income-tax rates across brackets.

Signed SB 1396 (Act 96, 2025) on May 27, 2025, creating a Green Fee funded by a 0.75% increase to the transient accommodations tax; the release says revenues will fund environmental stewardship, climate and hazard mitigation and sustainable tourism.

Signed SB 3025 (Act 220, 2026), creating a statewide program to buy and forgive medical debt for up to 50,000 residents (signing date not stated in the source; listed in the governor's July 15, 2026 end-of-session release).

Vetoed SB 3262 (2026, relating to education), saying it warranted further consideration because of the separation of responsibilities and duties between the Board of Education and the Hawaii Teacher Standards Board; the same July 15 release reports a line-item reduction to SB 2600, which makes a deposit into the emergency and budget reserve fund, before he signed it.

candidates.researchNotes: No direct source was found tying him to a stance on the fixed issue statements, so positions are omitted rather than inferred from party.

candidates.name: Gary Cordery
candidates.ballotNote: Running with Daniel Anthony for lieutenant governor.

summary.text: Gary Cordery is a Republican general contractor who has never held public office. He finished third in the 2022 Republican gubernatorial primary and won the 2026 nomination over Ken Fujiyama. His campaign emphasizes lower costs, tax cuts, permitting reform and government transparency.

background.text: Moved to Hawaii in 1981 and founded the contracting firm Kingdom Builders; has never held public office.
Co-founded the Aloha Freedom Coalition; finished third in the 2022 Republican primary for governor and in 2026 won the nomination.

priorities.text: Lower taxes and a smaller scope of government, including freezing senior property taxes and eliminating the general excise tax on food and medicine.
priorities.quote: We will reduce the taxes, fees and the scope of government.

priorities.text: Housing: using state land for about 15,000 fee-simple homes and creating an independent permit department.
More transparency: an office of transparency and audits and a ban on political donations from local unions and national PACs.

positions.summary: Proposes an independent state permit department, building about 15,000 fee-simple homes on state lands, and raising the share of zoned land from 5% to 6%.
Civil Beat reports he told the Honolulu Star-Advertiser in 2022 that if legislation to overturn abortion came to his desk as governor, he would sign it.
positions.quote: if legislation came to my desk as governor to overturn abortion, I would sign it.

candidates.researchNotes: Held no public office, so no record. Civil Beat's July Q&A did not address guns or public safety; the abortion position is as reported by Civil Beat (a 2022 Star-Advertiser statement), not from a campaign document. Statement on LNG added from the same Q&A; no campaign website found.

statements.quote: I am not necessarily opposed, but considering new technologies like Hydrogen, Fission and SNR's are solutions for the future.
statements.context: Civil Beat candidate Q&A, July 20, 2026, answering whether he supports a temporary transition to liquefied natural gas

researchNotes: Slate confirmed against the Hawaii Office of Elections' official sample general-election ballot (two tickets: Green/Kawakami D, Cordery/Anthony R). Some pre-primary lists show four nonpartisan gubernatorial filers, but none appears on the general-election ballot. Ballotpedia was blocked; Wikipedia is used only for basic biography. Primary percentages are omitted because news and Wikipedia figures conflict.
